akhfash:3-3.t: He said ﴿وَأَسَرُّواْ ٱلنَّجْوَى﴾: it is as though He said ﴿وَأَسَرُّواْ﴾ (and they kept secret) and then explained it afterwards, saying: "they are ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ﴾". Or this comes according to the dialect of those who say "ضَرَبُونِي قَوْمُكَ" (your people struck me, with the plural marker on the verb).

akhfash:30-30.t:
And He said ﴿أَنَّ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضَ كَانَتَا رَتْقاً﴾: He said ﴿كَانَتَا﴾ (dual) because He made them two kinds, like the Arabs' saying: "هُما لِقاحانِ سُودَان" (they are two black herds of milch camels), and in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُمْسِكُ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضَ أَن تَزُولاَ﴾. The poet said [in the ṭawīl metre; this is poetic witness no. 250]:
رَأَوْا جَبَلاً فَوْقَ الجِبالِ إِذا الْتَقَتْ * رُؤُوسُ كَبِيَرِيْهنَّ يَنْتَطِحَانِ
(They saw a mountain above the mountains: when the heads of their two great ones met, they butted each other.)
He said "رُؤوسُ" (heads, plural) and then said "يَنْتَطِحانِ" (dual). This is like the Arabs' saying "الجُزُراتِ" and "الطُرُقاَتِ" (plurals of plurals), so in this you may say "طُرُقانِ" for two (sets) and "جُزُرانِ" for two. The poet said [in the kāmil metre; this is poetic witness no. 251]:
وإِذاَ الرِّجَالُ رَأَوْا يَزِيدَ رَأَيْتَهُم * خُضْعَ الرِّقابِ نَواكِسِي الأَبْصارِ
(When men see Yazīd, you see them with humbled necks and downcast eyes.)
And the Arabs say "مَوَاليِات" and "صَواَحِبَاتُ يوسُف" (the female companions of Joseph). These have formed a broken plural and then pluralised "صَواحِب" again; in this way the masculine would be "صَواحِبُون", and its counterpart is "نَواكِسي". Some say "نواكِسِ" in the genitive position, as you say "حُجْرُ ضَبٍّ خَرِبٍ" (the burrow of a lizard, ruined, with the adjective genitive by proximity).

akhfash:37-37.t: And He said ﴿خُلِقَ ٱلإنْسَانُ مِنْ عَجَلٍ سَأُوْرِيكُمْ آيَاتِي فَلاَ تَسْتَعْجِلُونِ﴾: He means "from a hastening of the command", because He said: ﴿إِنَّمَا قَوْلُنَا لِشَيْءٍ إِذَآ أَرَدْنَاهُ أَن نَّقُولَ لَهُ كُنْ﴾. So this haste is like His word ﴿فَلاَ تَسْتَعْجِلُوهُ﴾, and His word ﴿فَلاَ تَسْتَعْجِلُونِ﴾, for ﴿سَأُوْرِيكُمْ آيَاتِي﴾.

akhfash:63-63.t: And He said ﴿فَاسْأَلُوهُمْ إِن كَانُواْ يِنْطِقُونَ﴾: He used the masculine (rational plural) for the idols though they are inanimate, because in their view they were among those who reason or speak.

akhfash:82-82.t:
And He said ﴿وَمِنَ ٱلشَّيَاطِينِ مَن يَغُوصُونَ لَهُ﴾: He used the masculine (rational plural) for the devils though they are not of humankind, except that they are like them in obedience and disobedience. Do you not see that you say "الشياطينُ يَعْصُونَ" (the devils disobey) and do not say "يَعْصِينَ" (feminine plural)? He made ﴿يَغُوصُونَ﴾ plural while ﴿مَنْ﴾ is singular in form, because ﴿مَنْ﴾ in meaning refers to a group. The poet said [in the kāmil metre; this is poetic witness no. 248]:
لَسْنَا كَمَنْ جَعَلَتْ إِيادٍ دارَهَا * تكريت تَنْظُرُ حَبَّها أَنْ يُحَصَدا
(We are not like those of Iyād who made Takrīt their home, waiting for their grain to be harvested.)
And he said [in the mutaqārib metre; this is poetic witness no. 249]:
أَطُوفُ بِهَا لاَ أَرَىَ غَيْرَهَا * كَمَا طافَ بالبِيْعَةِ الرّاهِبِ
(I circle around her, seeing no one else, as the monk circles round the church.)
He made "الراهبِ" a badal (substitute) for ﴿مَا﴾, as though he said "like the one who circled". «[Translator's note: ﴿مَا﴾ here refers to the «ما» of «كما» in the verse.]» And the Arabs say: "إِنَّ الحَقَّ مَنْ صَدَّقَ اللهَ" (the right is he who believes Allah), i.e. "the right is the right of him who believes Allah".

akhfash:87-87.t: And He said ﴿إِذ ذَّهَبَ مُغَاضِباً فَظَنَّ أَن لَّن نَّقْدِرَ عَلَيْهِ﴾, i.e. that We would not decree punishment for him, because he had sinned by leaving his people. He was angry only with some of the kings; he was not angry with his Lord — he knew Allah, Mighty and Majestic, better than that.
